To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Soluble splice variant of CTL‐A4 (s)CTLa4 binds to antigen presenting cells and inhibits expression of CD80 and CD86.
soluble CTLA4 (CTLA‐4) is able to suppress proliferation in autoreactive T‐cells but not in primary alloreactive cells.
sCTLA4 is able to suppress proliferation by autoreactive T cells, whereas CTLA‐4Ig and Lea29y are not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of CTLA4 in islet autoreactivity and its potential use in intervention therapy.
the role of CTLA4 in the pathogenesis of type 1 diabetes.
the identification of biomarkers of the disease process and with the development of new therapeutic strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sCTLA4 is a functional inhibitory molecule, whereas CTLA41g and LEA 29Y are not.
sCTLA4 is not involved in type 2 diabetes, but rather a marker of the disease.
the soluble CTLA4 splice variant (sCTLA‐4) does have the capacity to bind to antigen presenting cells and inhibit their co‐stimulatory capacity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CTLA4Igs are more efficient than soluble forms of CTLA4 in suppressing naive T cells, whereas sCTLA4 is more effective in suppressing memory T cell responses.
sCTLA4 may be an interesting target in type 1 autoimmune disease.

sCTLA4 is an important molecule for the regulation of autoreactive T cells, but not alloreactive T cells, whereas CTLA‐4‐Ig and LE‐A29Y are important for the regulation of alloreactive T‐cells, but not autoreactive T-cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sCTLA4 is a potent inhibitor of autoreactive T cells, whereas CTLA‐4Ig and its derivative LEA29Y are potent inhibitors of alloreactive T cells.
sCTLA4 is an effective inhibitor of memory autoreactive T cells, whereas CTLA‐Ig and LE29Y are more efficient in the primary immune response.
sCTLA4 is a potent inhibitor of autoreactive T cells, and therefore may be a good candidate as a therapeutic intervention for autoimmune diabetes.
